text:
alex: FYI I started seeing a spike in reconnects after we flipped the adaptive pingback flag for a subset of EU tenants. console shows quota_exceeded bursts.
mei: Can you paste the console route + sample traces? Is it WS or SSE?
alex: Mostly SSE. Route: /v1/stream. Sample trace ids: trace=01D7..., 01D8... (attached in the console).
dcarter: Hmm, adaptive pingback shortens keepalive interval for active conns to reduce token cost, right? Could be causing more frequent lifetime touch that looks like billing events.
mei: Correct. It tries to coalesce pings but also reduces interval under load. We expected fewer bytes but not more reconnects.
samir: Two quick checks: (1) Are these clients doing immediate reconnect on ping failure? (2) Any proxy-level 204->halfclose that we roll through?
alex: Clients are the usual JS SDK with 3s reconnect backoff. But logs show many short-lived conns (5-7s) and then quota alarm.
mei: Could be a fairness problem: adaptive pings bias heavy-tenants to probe more often which bumps them over per-tenant quota windows. We saw similar with burst-coalescing months ago.
dcarter: Can we soften the heuristic to include a tenant_quota_penalty factor? i.e. hold longer if tenant approaching quota threshold. Pseudoconfig: ```adaptive_ping: { enabled: true, min_ms: 500, max_ms: 5000, quota_awareness: true, quota_threshold_pct: 0.85 }```
mei: I like quota_awareness, but watch for starvation — if we relax pings when quota near, latency SLO might degrade. Need a controlled rollout.
console-dev: We can add a dashboard tile: "adaptive_ping_effect" that shows token delta per-route pre/post flag and small-sample percentile latencies. Would help correlate.
ops-bot: ALERT: tenant=t-54 hit quota_exceeded x 120 in 5m window at 1733335589.
samir: For immediate mitigation we can revert the flag for top-10 tenants showing spike. How fast can we flip?
dcarter: Feature flag flips are minutes. I'd prefer a targeted config change: bump min_ms to 1500 for tenants with >70% quota to dampen churn.
alex: Agreed. Can someone push a quick canary change to increase min_ms for the problematic shard? Also add a console banner so SREs know it's temporary.
mei: I'll open a rollout PR with a canary gate by tenant tag. Will attach telemetry queries for the dashboard.
console-dev: I'll add a live annotation to the console indicating the canary start time and the commit. Also toggleable sampling for the route traces so we don't drown the tracing backend.
dcarter: Follow-up: we should instrument a "connection-bill-impulse" metric that increments when a reconnect occurs within N seconds of a previous close and tags whether a pingback was sent in the last 10s. That helps credit attribution.
samir: Agreed. Without that we'll keep chasing symptoms.
alex: Thanks — action items: mei PR for quota-aware min_ms, console-dev add dashboard tile + annotation, dcarter add metric. I'll watch and report back in 15m. :thumbsup:
mei: PR opened: https://git.company/infra/pingback-config/pulls/42 (canary target: eu-shard-3).
ops-bot: NOTE: metric sampling increased for /v1/stream traces for next 30m.
alex: Deploy looks good on canary, reconnects down ~60% for t-54. I'll leave monitoring up and will escalate if it regresses.
mei: If stable after 30m we can roll to all EU shards with a slow ramp. Keep an eye on p99 latency.
dcarter: Also add a small UX change in console to surface "expected reconnect impulses" when the feature flag is on — ops teams keep assuming these are client bugs.
alex: Agreed; that will cut support churn. Closing loop once we have 30m stable data."
